title: Host-side prefill aggregator with affinity-aware submission
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Host-side work for prefill and decode paths is a dominant CPU overhead for short requests. We see high memcpy fanout, threadpool contention, and cross-socket memory traffic when many small requests prefill KV caches concurrently. Goal: reduce host CPU overhead by introducing a host-side prefill aggregation layer that coalesces small prefill uploads, routes batches to a socket-local submission queue, and circulates a compact pinned-buffer pool to reduce per-request malloc/mmap churn.

Scope: implement an aggregator that sits between the prefill assembler and GPU submission. The aggregator will: 1) receive lightweight prefill descriptors; 2) group descriptors by target GPU and NUMA socket; 3) coalesce small copys into a single scatter-gather transfer when beneficial; 4) submit to socket-local submission queues serviced by a small set of pinned threads; 5) recycle pinned buffers asynchronously to avoid free-time stalls.

Why different from existing work: unlike prior efforts focused on threadpool sizing or single-copy affinity, this ticket targets a mid-layer that understands prefill semantics and can trade a few microseconds of extra batching for substantial memory-copy reduction and lock contention relief. We emphasize NUMA awareness, scatter-gather coalescing, and pinned buffer lifecycle optimization rather than just kernel or scheduler tweaks.
proposed_design:
- Prefill descriptor: a lightweight struct containing request id, model id, target GPU id, list of source SG entries (pointer+len or iovec) and preferred deadline.
- Aggregator queues: one per GPU per NUMA node (socket-local). Each queue has two submission modes: immediate (for latency-critical prefills) and coalesced (accumulate up to X KB or Y ms).
- Buffer pool: per-socket pool of pinned, page-locked buffers allocated in that socket's NUMA domain. Pools expose try_reserve() which avoids blocking threads for allocation.
- Submission threads: small fixed-thread set pinned to the socket that drain queues, perform scatter-gather memcpy into pinned buffers (or use zero-copy if SG points are already pinned), and issue a single host->GPU transfer call.
- Backpressure: if pool is exhausted or queue depth crosses threshold, fall back to immediate single-request submit or degrade to direct path (existing prefill flow).
- Telemetry: counters for coalesced bytes, memcpy calls avoided, per-request latency delta, pool exhaustion events, and per-socket CPU utilization.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P0: end-to-end median prefill CPU time per short request reduced by >=30% in mixed short/medium workload compared to baseline.
2) P1: memcpy syscall count per 1k requests reduced by >=40% (measured in lab harness).
3) P2: no increase in 99th-percentile tail end-to-end latency by more than 5ms for latency-sensitive path when aggregator is enabled (immediate mode active).
4) P3: instrumentation shows >50% of small prefills are served via coalesced transfers under the target workload profile, and pinned buffer pool reuse rate >70%.
5) Automated unit and integration tests for buffer pool lifecycle, socket-local queueing, and fallback paths added and green in CI.
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype aggregator API and per-socket buffer pool. Add unit tests for allocation/recycle and NUMA placement.
Week 2: implement queueing semantics, simple coalescer that merges adjacent iovecs into a single pinned copy when total size < 128KB or delay < 2ms.
Week 3: integrate with runtime prefill codepath behind feature flag; add telemetry counters and initial microbench harness.
Week 4: run scaled benchmark (2000 qps mixed sizes) to tune thresholds; address contention hotspots; add end-to-end integration tests.
Rollout: Canary on runtime-2.3 for a small customer cohort, then staged ramp if metrics look stable.
test_plan: Unit tests: buffer pool concurrency, reservation/fallback semantics, queueing correctness.
Microbench: synthetic short-request workload to measure memcpy counts, CPU usage, and latency impact.
Regression: run existing decode/prefill regression suite to detect any correctness issues with KV cache population or ordering.
Canary: enable feature flag for 5% of production traffic with detailed telemetry, abort-on-error policy.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: coalescing introduces additional latency for some latency-sensitive requests. Mitigation: immediate-submission override and per-request deadline field honored; default thresholds tuned conservatively.
Risk: pinned buffer pool fragmentation or exhaustion. Mitigation: adaptive pool sizing heuristic and fallback to direct submits; expose runtime knob to admin for pool size limits.
Risk: NUMA misplacement causes cross-socket copies. Mitigation: allocate pinned buffers with libnuma affinity and add sanity checks in tests to ensure correct placement.
Risk: increased complexity and coupling with submission path. Mitigation: implement behind feature flag with clear rollback and health checks.
notes: We intentionally keep pool operations non-blocking for request threads; reserving can fail fast and trigger the existing direct submit path to preserve latency SLAs.
Coalescing heuristics should favor grouping items with similar deadlines and same model/gpu to avoid reordering effects on KV cache visibility.
We plan to reuse some buffer pool code from ENG-104321 but with NUMA-aware allocation and scatter-gather support.
Initial thresholds (128KB, 2ms) are placeholders — will tune with microbench results.
